sections.name: ReportFact, withoutCitations
sections.title: Fact shape and citation cleanup
sections.what: Defines what one fact looks like: a field name, its quote text, and the source IDs it belongs to. It also cuts citation markers off quote text by stopping at the first occurrence of the word cite.
sections.why: Keeps each fact's wording clean and tied to the right sources, as the header comment describes.
sections.watch_out: Any ordinary sentence containing the word cite will be cut short at that word.

sections.name: split
sections.title: Splitting text at a known word
sections.what: Splits a piece of text at a required separator word into two trimmed parts. If the separator is missing, it stops with an error.
sections.why: Lets one shared sentence be divided so each part goes to the right source.
sections.watch_out: A changed report wording makes the separator disappear, which stops the whole mapping. This is intended so bad data is not silently linked.

sections.name: scopedReportFacts (part 1)
sections.title: Facts for the first group of projects
sections.what: For a project key, builds the facts list. Single-source projects send all their text to one source ID. Mixed projects split shared text and assign each part to the source that publishes it, for example separating the Shuaibah schedule and participant text by the words it contains.
sections.why: The comments say that mixed rows must be split by exact cell or clause, rather than assigned to every source in the row.
sections.watch_out: Source S11 is used for both Agua Caliente and Topaz, so confirm that this is intended.

sections.name: scopedReportFacts (part 2)
sections.title: Facts for the remaining projects
sections.what: Continues the mapping for the AVSR1 and Mammoth projects. The Mammoth schedule must split into exactly three parts, and any project key not in the list is rejected with an error.
sections.why: The explicit error for unknown keys means a new project must be added on purpose, rather than appearing with guessed sources.
sections.watch_out: The Mammoth schedule check is strict, so any extra or missing schedule clause in the report will stop the import.

summary: Maps each solar project's report facts to the correct register source IDs, using exact wording from the report and failing if the expected wording is not found.
purpose: Makes sure each quoted fact is linked to the source that actually publishes it, instead of attaching a whole mixed row to every source.
why: The header comment says the report's named publishers decide attribution, and page fetches do not upgrade these excerpts to verified quotes.
how: For a given project key, the function creates a list of facts. Simple projects use one source ID throughout. Projects with mixed sources split the shared text at known words and assign each part to its own source.
inputs: A project key, a list of identity and capacity text cells, and a list of detail text cells taken from the report.
outputs: A list of facts, each with a field name, cleaned quote text, and the source IDs it belongs to.
risks: The splitting words are fixed in the code, so a change in the report's wording stops the import. Unknown project keys are rejected on purpose.
debug: When the error says a clause boundary is missing, compare the report wording with the separator text in the matching case. When the error says no mapping exists, check that the project key is spelled exactly as in the code.
